Roosevelt Reservoir, Fort Peck Lake, Lake Sakakawea, Lake Oahe, Lake Powell, and Lake Mead. These reservoirs provide water supply, hydroelectric power, recreation, and wildlife habitat, and are operated by various government agencies and organizations. Here is a summary of the text in 2-3 sentences:

Lake Mead is the largest manmade lake in the US, with a capacity of 28.76 million acre-feet at full pool. It was created by the Hoover Dam on the Colorado River and supplies water to over 25 million people in Nevada, Arizona, California, and Mexico. The lake faces challenges from drought and urbanization, but conservation measures and innovative solutions are being implemented to ensure its survival.
